key_insight: PoreML is an open-source, pore-scale physics workflow that combines GPU-based simulation data generation with unified ML training and evaluation to predict multiphase flow in porous media.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets practical design and reliability needs in CO2 storage, fuel cells, and packaging by enabling faster surrogate models for complex fluid transport in real microstructures.
method: GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver for reproducible pore-scale multiphase flow simulation
3.3 TB dataset with 560 runs and 158,546 time steps spanning synthetic and micro-CT-derived geometries
Unified benchmarking for one-step prediction, autoregressive rollout, and physical-consistency checks
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 3.3 TB dataset and five evaluated models, with protocols that test both predictive accuracy and physical consistency plus transfer to larger and micro-CT-derived domains.
watch_item: Performance may still be limited by data availability and domain shift when models are transferred to larger geometries or to real micro-CT structures.
paper_title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
